newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: German in 48-hour Irish siege over eviction.
newsitem.headline: German in 48-hour Irish siege over eviction.

text.p: A German who barricaded himself in an Irish cottage after shooting three people to protest against his eviction was holding police at bay on Thursday for a second day.
Gerrit Isenborges, 41, from Duesseldorf, told police surrounding the cottage that his terminally-ill mother, 82, had died inside since the siege began on Wednesday.
Isenborges shot and wounded three council officers when they tried to serve a notice evicting him from the cottage near Ballyconnel in County Cavan. None of them was seriously hurt.
Police said they had no intention of storming the house and hoped the incident would end peacefully.

Isenborges has lived in the area for about three years after working as a caretaker at a nearby "Wild West" theme park. The cottage's owner, Austrian Michael Hehle, who also owns the theme park, sought his eviction.
Hehle told Irish media that Isenborges failed to carry out agreed repairs to the cottasge or pay any bills.
